## Preliminaries

**Working scope (declared as assumption, not fact).** Jonah 3:1-10 is taken as a single reading unit — the second commission, Jonah's compliance, and Nineveh's repentance together with God's response, forming one continuous arc with no internal break. This chapter opens by directly repeating 1:1-3's call-formula almost verbatim, and is read throughout with that parallel actively in view. "Bearing on the inner being" here includes: (a) Jonah's own interior, again largely unstated at precisely the moments (compliance, proclamation) where it might most be expected — a contrast with ch. 2's fullness; (b) the people of Nineveh, both as a collective (3:5, 3:10) and via the individuated king (3:6-9) and his nobles (3:7); (c) God's own stated operations (seeing, relenting, withholding), in scope per note (b), and here for the first time in the book placed in direct, textually-anchored comparison with a human operation via shared vocabulary (Q12).

**Reading rule applied.** No [AMBIGUOUS]-span STEP-live resolution was needed — the base extract reports 100% meaning coverage for this range (121/121 non-particle spans). Hebrew narrative prose. This is the first passage debate written under the new Q12/B.11 addition, applied per its own discipline: recorded only where the passage's data anchors it, not force-searched into every verse.

**Corpus-continuity check.** Performed before writing. Read: `WA-jonah-1-debate.md` and `WA-jonah-2-debate.md` in full. Continuity: Jon 1 closed with the LORD's word/command (1:1-2) triggering Jonah's flight; Jon 2 closed with Jonah's deliverance (2:10) and flagged Jon 3 — itself a close textual parallel to 1:1-2 — as the natural next passage. Confirmed here: 3:1-2 nearly repeat 1:1-2 verbatim, flagged in full below as a direct comparison.

## Per-verse debate

### Jon 3:1

> Then the word of the Lord came to Jonah the second time, saying,

**Observation.** "The word [H1697G] of the LORD [H3068G] came [H1961] to [H0413] Jonah [H3124] the second time [H8145], saying [H0559/H9005]."

**Operation 1 — the LORD's word coming to Jonah again.**
- **Action-type:** came/was-given (a word-event, recurring).
- **Subject:** the LORD.
- **Operation:** a movement — the word "coming to" Jonah, explicitly marked as a second occurrence.
- **Source:** self.
- **Target:** Jonah.

**Interrogative — questions considered.** (`WA-interpretation-questions` Q1-Q12 — every human mentioned in this verse is a presumptive candidate, per read-guidance step 2 note (f); a candidate that resolves to nothing is recorded as an explicit silence, per Part B.4, not omitted)
- Q1/Q2: Jonah — focused inner being; again nothing of his reception is stated. After ch. 2's extended prayer, this silence reads differently than at 1:1 — he has shown he can speak at length, yet here again says nothing.
- Q3: The recurrence itself is stated ("the second time") — a deliberate narrative marker. Jonah's reception is unstated.
- Q4: Source = the LORD, self.
- Q5: Target = Jonah.
- Q6: Movement.
- Q7: **Direct near-repetition of 1:1**, explicitly flagged by the text itself as "the second time" — inviting direct comparison of the two commissions and their very different initial outcomes.
- Q8: N/A.
- Q9: Sufficient.
- Q11: came/was-given (recurring).
- Q12: N/A this verse — no juxtaposed divine/human operation within the verse itself to compare; the comparison is with 1:1, a cross-passage linkage already tracked under Q7.

**Decision.** Retain; flagged as the direct near-repetition of 1:1, opening the second commission.

### Jon 3:3

> So Jonah arose and went to Nineveh, according to the word of the Lord. Now Nineveh was an exceedingly great city, three days ’ journey in breadth.

**Observation.** "Jonah [H3124] arose [H6965B] and went [H1980G] to Nineveh [H5210], according to [H9004] the word [H1697G] of the LORD [H3068G]. Nineveh [H5210] was [H1961] an exceedingly [H0430G/H9005] great [H1419A] city [H5892B], three [H7969] days' [H3117G] journey [H4109] in breadth."

**Operation 1 — Jonah's compliance.**
- **Action-type:** arose/went (complied).
- **Subject:** Jonah.
- **Operation:** a movement — going to Nineveh, explicitly "according to the word of the LORD."
- **Source:** self, but explicitly stated as compliance with the LORD's command — the first time in the book Jonah is shown obeying a divine command without qualification.
- **Target:** Nineveh.

**Operation 2 — description of Nineveh's scale.**
- **Action-type:** n/a (descriptive).
- **Subject:** Nineveh, the city itself.
- **Operation:** a state — its own scale, "an exceedingly great city, three days' journey."
- **Source:** n/a.
- **Target:** n/a — background information, in scope per note (d)'s own qualifier since it directly bears on the humans about to be described (its scale explains 3:4's partial-day proclamation).

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Jonah — his compliance is stated as an act; his own interior in finally complying (relief? resignation? continued reluctance, given ch. 4's later outburst?) is not stated — a genuine, notable silence at exactly the moment his obedience is first recorded.
- Q3: The compliance is stated, explicitly marked as obedience ("according to the word of the LORD"), unlike 1:3's flight. Jonah's interior in complying is unstated.
- Q4: Source of the compliance = self, explicitly aligned with the LORD's word (linkage).
- Q5: Target = Nineveh.
- Q6: Movement (Jonah); state (the city's description).
- Q7: **Major reversal-linkage to 1:3**: where 1:3 narrated Jonah rising to flee ("Jonah rose to flee... from the presence of the LORD"), 3:3 narrates Jonah rising to comply ("Jonah arose and went... according to the word of the LORD") — same initial verb (arose, H6965), opposite direction and outcome, left by the text to speak for itself.
- Q8: N/A this verse (the city description is not itself an operation on a human collective, though it sets up 3:5's collective).
- Q9: Sufficient; Jonah's own interior in complying is named as an insufficiency — especially significant given ch. 4 later reveals substantial residual reluctance/anger, raising whether this compliance is glad, grudging, or merely dutiful.
- Q11: arose/went (complied).
- Q12: N/A directly this verse (though this compliance, contrasted with 1:3's flight, could later be weighed against the human "turning" language of 3:8-10 — held for the passage-level linkages, not asserted here).

**Decision.** Retain both. Flagged as the major reversal-linkage against 1:3, and Jonah's unstated interior in complying flagged as a significant open question feeding directly into ch. 4.

- **Subject:** Jonah.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Jonah — his own interior while delivering this message (reluctant? resigned? hopeful? matter-of-fact?) is not stated — the shortest, starkest prophetic proclamation in the book, delivered with zero recorded emotional coloring, in stark contrast to the extended first-person interior he gave in ch. 2's prayer.
- Q3: The act and its quoted content are stated. Jonah's interior in delivering it is unstated.

- Q11: proclaimed.
- Q12: N/A directly.

**Decision.** Retain. Jonah's total absence of stated feeling while delivering the one message the whole book turns on is flagged as a significant, deliberate-seeming silence (emergent question).

### Jon 3:5

> And the people of Nineveh believed God. They called for a fast and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them to the least of them.

**Observation.** "The people [H0582] of Nineveh [H5210] believed [H0539] God [H0430G]. They called [H7121G] for a fast [H6685] and put on [H3847] sackcloth [H8242], from the greatest [H1419A/H9006] of them to the least [H6996A/H9028/H5704/H9002] of them."

**Operation 1 — Nineveh's collective belief.**
- **Action-type:** believed.
- **Subject:** "the people of Nineveh" — a human collective, credited directly with a stated interior act.
- **Operation:** a state — a stated interior disposition: belief in God, in immediate response to Jonah's proclamation.
- **Source:** Jonah's proclamation (3:4), and behind it God's own word (3:1-2) — a direct linkage, though the verse itself credits the belief to the people's own response.
- **Target:** God ("believed God").

**Operation 2 — Nineveh's collective mourning acts.**
- **Action-type:** fasted/mourned (called a fast, put on sackcloth).
- **Subject:** the people of Nineveh, "from the greatest... to the least" — an explicit merism spanning the whole social hierarchy.
- **Operation:** a movement — communal acts of repentance/mourning.
- **Source:** self, motivated by the stated belief (Operation 1, direct linkage).
- **Target:** n/a directly (self-directed acts of humiliation); relationally, God (the implied recipient of the mourning-signal).

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: "The people of Nineveh" — a human collective, focused inner being per note (c)/(f); here, remarkably, their belief is stated directly and immediately, with no hedge, inference, or delay — one of the most immediate, unambiguous stated-interior responses in this corpus so far (contrast the sailors' own gradual arc across many verses in ch. 1).
- Q3: Stated, explicitly — "the people of Nineveh believed God" — not inferred.
- Q4: Source of the belief = Jonah's proclamation/God's word (linkage). Source of the fasting/sackcloth = their own stated belief (a clean, in-verse enablement chain).
- Q5: Target of the belief = God; target of the mourning-acts = n/a directly stated, though implicitly directed toward God.
- Q6: State (belief) issuing in movement (fasting, sackcloth).
- Q7: **Major linkage**: the single most immediate belief-response to a divine word anywhere in the book — contrast Jonah's own initial response to the identical word-formula at 1:1-3 (flight) and even the sailors' own gradual, multi-verse arc (1:5-16). Nineveh believes and acts within one verse, no delay, no negotiation.
- Q8: "The people of Nineveh," explicitly spanning "the greatest... to the least" — an emphatically total collective, reshaping the operation as a movement across the entire social body, no exception named.
- Q9: Sufficient.
- Q11: believed; fasted/mourned.
- Q12: N/A directly this verse (the belief responds to a divine word, but is not itself a like-for-like operation juxtaposed against a stated divine operation — held for the passage-level linkages, per B.11's discipline against forcing the comparison).

**Decision.** Retain both operations — flagged as the passage's most immediate, unqualified inner-being response to a divine word in the corpus so far.

### Jon 3:6

> The word reached the king of Nineveh, and he arose from his throne, removed his robe, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.

**Observation.** "The word [H1697G] reached [H5060] the king [H4428G] of Nineveh [H5210], and he arose [H6965B] from his throne [H3678G], removed [H5674C] his robe [H0155], covered [H3680] himself with sackcloth [H8242], and sat [H3427] in ashes [H0665]."

**Operation 1 — the word's reaching the king.**
- **Action-type:** reached (touched, arrived).
- **Subject:** "the word" — the report of Nineveh's response, reaching the king specifically, now individuated from the general population of 3:5.
- **Operation:** a movement — arrival, "reached the king."
- **Source:** the general report of Nineveh's response (implied, following 3:5) — a subtle shift from direct address (3:4) to indirect report reaching the throne.
- **Target:** the king of Nineveh — an individuated human, distinct from "the people" of 3:5.

**Operation 2 — the king's own response.**
- **Action-type:** arose/humbled-himself (removed robe, covered in sackcloth, sat in ashes).
- **Subject:** the king of Nineveh — individuated, per note (f), a specific human now singled out from the collective.
- **Operation:** a movement — a sequence of humbling acts, escalating in humility from throne to ashes.
- **Source:** self, in direct continuation of the report reaching him (linkage).
- **Target:** n/a directly (self-directed acts of humiliation).

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: The king — a newly individuated focused inner being, distinct from the general "people" of 3:5; his acts are a stated, escalating sequence, though his own stated disposition (fear? conviction? grief?) is not given in first-person terms — only the acts, which strongly imply humility/repentance.
- Q3: The acts are stated explicitly. The king's own interior disposition behind them is inferred from the acts themselves (a strong, textually-supported inference — conventional mourning/humiliation gestures — but not a first-person stated confession, distinguishing this from Jonah's own stated confessions at Jon 1:9/1:12).
- Q4: Source of the king's response = self, enabled/motivated by the word reaching him (linkage, Operation 1).
- Q5: Target = n/a directly (self-directed).
- Q6: Movement, both operations.
- Q7: Direct linkage to 3:5 (the general population's response, now paralleled and escalated by the king individually) and forward to 3:7 (his formal decree, making the response official/binding on the whole city).
- Q8: N/A — the king is here individuated, distinct from the collective of 3:5.
- Q9: Sufficient for the acts; the king's own stated disposition is an inference, not a first-person statement — named, not overstated.
- Q11: arose/humbled-himself.
- Q12: N/A directly.

**Decision.** Retain both operations. The king's disposition is recorded as a strong, textually-supported inference from his acts, not a stated confession — kept distinct per Part B.3.

**Observation.** "He issued a proclamation [H2199/H0559] and published [H0559/H9005/H9023] through Nineveh [H5210/H9003], 'By [H9006] the decree [H2940] of the king [H4428G] and his nobles [H1419A/H9002]: let neither man [H0120G] nor beast [H0929], herd [H1241] nor flock [H6629G], taste [H2938] anything [H3972]. **Operation 1 — the king's formal decree.**
- **Action-type:** decreed/proclaimed.
- **Subject:** the king, jointly with "his nobles" — a second, distinct party named alongside him.
- **Operation:** a movement — a formal, city-wide proclamation, making the king's own personal humbling (3:6) into binding public policy.
- **Source:** self (the king, jointly with his nobles) — a shift from personal, individuated response (3:6) to formal, collective authority.
- **Target:** "Nineveh" (the whole city, addressed formally); specifically, "man... beast, herd... flock" — an unusually inclusive scope, extending the fast even to animals.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**

"His nobles" — a second, distinct human party, named jointly with the king but not separately analysed for their own interior in this verse — a candidate silence, not resolved here.

### Jon 3:8

> but let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and let them call out mightily to God. Let everyone turn from his evil way and from the violence that is in his hands.

**Observation.** "Let man [H0120G] and beast [H0929] be covered [H3680] with sackcloth [H8242], and let them call out [H7121G] mightily [H2394/H9003] to God [H0430G]. Let everyone [H0376I] turn [H7725O] from his evil [H7451I] way [H1870G], and from [H4480A] the violence [H2555] that is in his hands [H3709G/H0834A]."

**Operation 1 — the decreed universal mourning.**
- **Action-type:** covered/mourned (decreed extension of sackcloth to all, including animals).
- **Subject:** "man and beast" — continuing the maximal scope from 3:7.
- **Operation:** a movement/state — decreed covering in sackcloth.
- **Source:** the king's decree (3:7, direct linkage).
- **Target:** n/a directly (decreed condition).

**Operation 2 — the decreed collective cry to God.**
- **Action-type:** cried-out (mightily, to God).
- **Subject:** "them" (man and beast, per the decree's own continuing scope) — a cry "to God" from beasts being a striking, unexplained detail (see insufficiencies).
- **Operation:** a movement — decreed, urgent petition.
- **Source:** the decree (continuing).
- **Target:** God.

**Operation 3 — the decreed universal moral turning.**
- **Action-type:** turned (repented — H7725, the same root used of God's own turning at 3:9).
- **Subject:** "everyone" — an individuating universal, decreed to turn "from his evil way and from the violence that is in his hands."
- **Operation:** a movement — a moral reorientation, decreed at the level of individual conduct, not merely collective ritual.
- **Source:** the decree (continuing), though the actual turning, if it occurs, is each individual's own act.
- **Target:** each person's own "evil way"/"violence."

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: "Man"/"everyone" — a human collective and, within it, an emphatically individuated universal ("everyone... his evil way... his hands") — per note (c)/(f), the decree treats repentance as something each person must individually do, not merely a collective ritual; this is a stated moral demand, not yet a stated fulfillment.
- Q3: The decree's content is stated, in full, direct quotation. Whether it is actually carried out by "everyone" individually is not confirmed until 3:10's summary.
- Q4: Source of the decree = the king (continuing 3:7). The turning itself, if it happens, is sourced to each individual.
- Q5: Target = "his evil way... the violence that is in his hands" — each person's own conduct.
- Q6: Movement — decreed as both ritual (sackcloth, crying out) and moral (turning from evil/violence), the text explicitly distinguishing ritual mourning from moral reformation, naming both, not conflating them.
- Q7: **Direct linkage to 3:9-10** — the same root (H7725, "turn") used here of the Ninevites' decreed turning recurs, applied to GOD's own turning, at 3:9 and again at 3:10.
- Q8: "Man and beast... everyone" — the decree spans from the collective-maximal (man and beast together) to the individuated-universal (everyone, his own hands) — two different collective grains in the same verse.
- Q9: Sufficient for the decree's content; whether beasts can meaningfully "cry out to God" or "turn from violence" is not explained by the text — named as a striking, unresolved detail, not filled from outside convention.
- Q11: covered/mourned; cried-out; turned (repented).
- Q12: **Yes — textually anchored.** The decreed human "turning" (H7725) directly mirrors, in shared vocabulary, God's own "turning" at 3:9-10 (also H7725). Recorded here per Q12/B.11's discipline: the anchor is the shared root itself; no further theological elaboration is added.

**Decision.** Retain all three operations. Flagged prominently as this passage's clearest instance of Q12 (divine mirroring, shared root H7725 between human and divine "turning").

### Jon 3:9

> Who knows? God may turn and relent and turn from his fierce anger, so that we may not perish.”

**Observation.** "Who knows [H3045/H4310]? God [H0430G] may turn [H7725O] and relent [H5162H], and turn [H7725O] from his fierce [H2740] anger [H0639G], so that we may not [H3808] perish [H0006]."

**Operation 1 — the king's expressed hope.**
- **Action-type:** hoped (expressed uncertain hope — "who knows?").
- **Subject:** the king, continuing as speaker of the decree from 3:7-8.
- **Operation:** a state — a stated, explicitly uncertain hope, not a claim of assured outcome.
- **Source:** self.
- **Target:** n/a directly (a general hope); relationally, God (the hoped-for actor).

**Operation 2 — God's hoped-for turning, relenting, and turning from anger.**
- **Action-type:** turned/relented (hoped-for, not yet narrated as having occurred).
- **Subject:** God — explicitly named as the one who "may turn and relent and turn from his fierce anger."
- **Operation:** a state/movement — a hoped-for change, described using the SAME verb (H7725, "turn") the decree has just demanded of the Ninevites (3:8) — a direct, textually-anchored parallel.
- **Source:** self — God's own hoped-for, freely-exercised change of mind; the king does not claim to compel or earn this ("who knows" explicitly denies certainty or entitlement).
- **Target:** "his fierce anger" (the object of the turning); implicitly, the city ("so that we may not perish").

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: The king — his own hope is stated directly, in his own voice, explicitly hedged ("who knows?") — a notable contrast to Jonah's own certainty about the LORD's character, later stated at Jon 4:2 (outside this passage, a forward-pointer). God — described here by the king, a human character, not the narrator — a genuine question about divine action, held as the king's own hope/interpretation (Part B.3), not a narratorial doctrine.
- Q3: The king's hope is stated, explicitly hedged. Whether God actually does turn is not yet stated (resolved at 3:10).
- Q4: Source of the king's hope = self. Source of God's hoped-for turning = God, self (as the king describes it) — the king attributes no external compulsion or cause to God's own potential change of mind.
- Q5: Target = God's "fierce anger" (the object turned from); the city (beneficiary).
- Q6: State (hope) and a hoped-for state/movement (God's turning).
- Q7: **Q12 (divine mirroring), directly anchored**: "turn" (H7725) is used twice in this single verse of GOD's own hoped-for action, immediately following its use of the Ninevites' decreed turning at 3:8 — the same root, applied first to the human side (3:8, decreed) and then to the divine side (3:9, hoped-for) of the same reconciliation. Also linkage forward to 3:10 (where the hoped-for turning is confirmed as having actually occurred).
- Q8: N/A — the king speaks individually here, on behalf of the city ("we"), a collective interest without itself being an operation on a named collective in this verse.
- Q9: Sufficient.
- Q11: hoped (who knows); turned/relented (hoped-for, God).
- Q12: **Yes — the passage's clearest anchored instance.** Human turning (3:8, decreed) and divine turning (3:9, hoped-for) share the identical root H7725, spoken back-to-back. Recorded as the observation itself; not elaborated into a general claim about how the two turnings compare in kind — the Ninevites' turning-from-evil is a moral change, God's turning-from-anger is a disposition/action change — a difference named, not resolved, per B.11.

**Decision.** Retain both operations — flagged as the single clearest, most concentrated Q12 instance in the passage.

### Jon 3:10

> When God saw what they did, how they turned from their evil way, God relented of the disaster that he had said he would do to them, and he did not do it.

**Observation.** "God [H0430G] saw [H7200G] what they did [H4639K/H0853], how they turned [H7725O/H9028/H3588A] from their evil [H7451I] way [H1870G]. God [H0430G] relented [H5162H] of the disaster [H7451C] that he had said [H1696G] he would do [H6213A] to them, and he did not [H3808] do [H6213A] it."

**Operation 1 — God's seeing.**
- **Action-type:** saw/observed.
- **Subject:** God.
- **Operation:** a movement/state — an act of divine attention, directed at Nineveh's conduct.
- **Source:** self.
- **Target:** "what they did, how they turned from their evil way" — the Ninevites' own collective act, confirming retrospectively that the decree of 3:7-8 was actually carried out, not merely proclaimed.

**Operation 2 — the Ninevites' confirmed turning.**
- **Action-type:** turned (repented, confirmed as having actually occurred).
- **Subject:** "they" (the Ninevites, collective).
- **Operation:** a movement — the same H7725 "turn" now confirmed as an actual, completed act, not merely a decreed intention.
- **Source:** self — their own act, now stated as having actually happened.
- **Target:** "their evil way."

**Operation 3 — God's relenting and withholding of the disaster.**
- **Action-type:** relented/withheld (did not do it).
- **Subject:** God.
- **Operation:** a movement — a change in God's own prior stated intention, now explicitly not carried out.
- **Source:** self — directly and explicitly sourced to Operation 1 (God's own seeing of their turning): see → relent → withhold, one of the cleanest, most explicit causal chains in the whole book.
- **Target:** Nineveh (the beneficiary; the disaster withheld from them).

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: The Ninevites — their turning, only decreed at 3:8 and hoped-for at 3:9, is now explicitly confirmed as an actual, completed collective act, closing the open question left at 3:8-9. God — described here by the NARRATOR (not, as at 3:9, by the king's own speech) as actually relenting and withholding judgment — the narratorial voice now confirms what the king could only hope for.
- Q3: All three operations stated, explicitly, by the narrator — the strongest, most direct statement of divine responsiveness to human moral change anywhere in the book.
- Q4: Source of God's seeing = self. Source of the Ninevites' turning = their own act, now confirmed. Source of God's relenting = explicitly, directly stated as God's own response to what God saw — Part B.5's state/enablement distinction is not even needed here since both the state and its source are fully and explicitly given.
- Q5: Target of God's seeing = the Ninevites' conduct; target of the relenting = the disaster, withheld from Nineveh.
- Q6: Movement, all three operations.
- Q7: **Culminating linkage completing the chapter's arc**: 3:8 (decreed turning) → 3:9 (the king's hoped-for divine turning, hedged as uncertain) → 3:10 (both turnings confirmed as having actually happened, by the narrator's own authoritative voice, resolving the king's "who knows" into stated fact).
- Q8: "They" (the Ninevites) — collective, continuing from 3:5-9.
- Q9: Sufficient.
- Q11: saw/observed; turned (confirmed); relented/withheld.
- Q12: **Yes — the passage's culminating, fully-confirmed instance.** Both the human turning and the divine relenting-from-anger are narrated together in this one verse as accomplished realities, closing the arc opened at 3:8's decree and 3:9's hope. Recorded as the passage's clearest example of what Q12 exists to surface; not elaborated beyond naming the parallel and its resolution.

**Decision.** Retain all three operations — flagged as the culminating fulfillment of the passage's central Q12 instance (human turning / divine turning, both confirmed).

## Passage-level linkages (Q7)

1. **3:1-2 directly repeat 1:1-2's call-formula** almost verbatim, explicitly marked "the second time" (3:1) — inviting direct comparison of the two commissions and their opposite initial outcomes (flight vs. compliance).
2. **3:2's withheld content** ("the message that I tell you") contrasts with 1:2's stated content ("for their evil has come up before me") — a deliberate narrative variation, not explained.
3. **3:3's "Jonah arose and went... according to the word of the LORD"** directly reverses 1:3's "Jonah rose to flee... from the presence of the LORD" — same initial verb (arose), opposite direction and outcome, left by the text to speak for itself.
4. **Q12 — the passage's central instance, textually anchored by shared vocabulary (H7725, "turn")**: the Ninevites' decreed turning from evil (3:8) and God's own hoped-for turning from anger (3:9) share the identical root, spoken back to back; both are then confirmed as accomplished fact together in 3:10 — the clearest example so far of the new divine-mirroring dimension. Recorded as the shared-word observation itself, not elaborated into a general claim about how the two turnings compare in kind (moral reorientation vs. change of disposition/action — a difference named, not resolved, per B.11).
5. **Nineveh's collective response (3:5)** — immediate, unqualified belief — contrasts sharply with both Jonah's own initial response to the identical word (1:1-3, flight) and the sailors' gradual, multi-verse arc (1:5-16) — the fastest, most complete inner-being turnaround in the book so far, achieved by the book's outsiders, not its prophet.
6. **The king's individuated humbling (3:6) and formal decree (3:7-8)** parallel, in miniature, the earlier captain's individuated role among the sailors (1:6) — both scenes feature one named/titled figure acting representatively for a larger collective.

## Insufficiencies register

- Whether the exact five-word proclamation of 3:4 is the LORD's own given wording or Jonah's own compression of "the message" (3:2) is not stated.
- Jonah's own interior in finally complying (3:3) and in delivering the proclamation (3:4) is not stated — a significant silence, especially given ch. 4's later disclosure of his continuing reluctance.
- The nobles' own disposition, though named as co-authors of the decree (3:7), is not separately stated.
- How or whether beasts can meaningfully "cry out to God" or "turn from violence" (3:8) is not explained by the text.
- Why 3:2 withholds the message's content (unlike 1:2) is not stated.

## Emergent questions log (filed against this passage — not merged across passages; resolved, if at all, at the whole-book read)

- **EQ11.** Jonah's total silence about his own interior at the moment of his compliance (3:3) and proclamation (3:4) — his most consequential prophetic act in the book — is at least as striking as ch. 1's silences, and now sits directly alongside ch. 4's later revelation that his compliance was not glad. Does the narrative's silence here anticipate that later disclosure, withholding it deliberately? Carried forward to ch. 4.
- **EQ12 (Q12 seed for future passages).** Now that Q12 has one clearly anchored instance (H7725, "turn," 3:8-10), is this kind of shared-root divine/human mirroring a recurring device in this corpus, or unusual to this passage? Carried forward — to be watched for, not searched for, in future debates (per B.11's discipline).
- **EQ13.** Nineveh's total, immediate, unqualified turning (3:5-10) is never given a stated reason beyond the proclamation itself (3:4) — no fear-of-specific-threat detail, no named leader's persuasion beyond the king's own later decree. Is the speed/completeness of the response itself meant to be read as remarkable, implicitly setting up Jonah's own contrasting anger in ch. 4? Carried forward to the whole-book read.

## Open decisions / next steps

- Next passage: Jonah 4 (Jonah's anger, and the LORD's closing rebuke) — the final chapter, and the natural place several of this debate's open threads (Jonah's unstated compliance-disposition, EQ11) are expected to resolve or at least be directly engaged.
- EQ11-EQ13 carried forward per B.9/B.8, not resolved here.
